summary: Today’s pulse tracks Reeves says planning for energy bills support under way but hints wealthiest may not be included – UK politics live, Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon, and Texas residents feel homes shake miles away from oil refinery explosion. Across Guardian and NPR, the strongest repeated signals are before, injured, and local. In the background, Middle East crisis live: Pakistan reportedly favouring Vance for role in possible US-Iran peace talks and LaGuardia pilots raised safety alarms months before deadly runway crash keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Reeves says planning for energy bills support under way but hints wealthiest may not be included – UK politics live
headlines.description: Chancellor says she has the data available to run targeted scheme, unlike the Tory programme used when the Ukraine war started The live feed from the Lib Dem local elections campaign launch did not last long, and it did not include footage of Ed Davey taking questions from reporters. But this is what the Lib Dems are saying about their five key campaign issues. -Cut the cost of living: A plan to halve energy bills within a decade, saving households an average of £870 a year - Fix the NHS and care: Guarantee the right to see a GP within seven days (or 24 hours for urgent cases) and ending 12-hour A&E waits. - Rescue high streets: Give an emergency cut to VAT for hospitality businesses, to bring prices down and boost struggling high streets. - Clean up rivers: Ban water companies from dumping raw sewage into local rivers and coastal areas. - Restore community policing: Ensure visible, effective local policing to reduce crime.

headlines.title: Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon
headlines.description: Pulido has been a mainstay of Tejano music —a genre blending traditional regional Mexican elements with country, pop and conjunto influences — for more than three decades.

headlines.title: Texas residents feel homes shake miles away from oil refinery explosion
headlines.description: Images and videos online showed large plume of smoke and flames billowing out from refinery, but no one was injured No one was injured in Monday’s explosion at the Valero refinery in Port Arthur, about 90 miles (145km) east of Houston, said Charlotte M Moses. The Port Arthur mayor had urged residents in parts of the west side of the city to stay put.

headlines.title: Middle East crisis live: Pakistan reportedly favouring Vance for role in possible US-Iran peace talks
headlines.description: Pakistan’s military attempting to broker negotiations between US and Iran Pakistan’s army chief attempts to broker Iran peace talks in call with Trump In Australia, the number of petrol stations running out of fuel continues to climb as the Middle East war drags on, with at least 184 dry across the country’s three most populous states . On Tuesday, 51 service stations in the state of New South Wales were out of fuel and 164 out of diesel, compared with 38 and 131 respectively the previous day, premier Chris Minns said.

headlines.title: LaGuardia pilots raised safety alarms months before deadly runway crash
headlines.description: Nasa reports show repeated warnings of close calls before crash that killed two pilots and injured 41 others According to the aviation safety reporting system administered by the US space agency Nasa, a pilot using the airport in the summer wrote, “Please do something,” after air traffic controllers failed to provide appropriate guidance about multiple nearby aircraft.

headlinePool.title: UK medical council overhaul may mean more doctors struck off for racism and antisemitism
headlinePool.description: Health department says ‘too many’ doctors have been using racist language, particularly on social media, without swift action An overhaul of the General Medical Council is expected to lead to more doctors that face accusations of racism and antisemitism on social media being struck off. The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has launched a consultation on changes to the legislation governing the regulation of doctors, saying the move will lead to the biggest reform of the medical regulator, the GMC, in four decades.

headlinePool.title: ‘Extraordinary event’ for mountain gorillas as new twins born in DRC
headlinePool.description: Conservationists celebrate second twin birth just two months after another found in Virunga national park A second set of mountain gorilla twins has been born in Virunga national park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), in what conservationists are celebrating as an “extraordinary” event for the endangered primates. Just two months after tiny twin mountain gorillas were discovered by rangers in the Virunga massif, in eastern DRC, another rare twin birth has been found by park wardens. This time, an infant male and female have been spotted in the Baraka family, a troop of 19 mountain gorillas that roam the region’s high-altitude rainforests.

headlinePool.title: ‘It won’t be pretty!’ French and Saunders to play the Ugly Sisters in Palladium panto
headlinePool.description: Comedy duo will take the stage together in the West End for the first time in 17 years in Cinderella alongside Julian Clary Dawn French and Jennifer Saunders are to return to the stage together for the first time in 17 years to play the Ugly Sisters in the London Palladium pantomime. “It won’t be pretty,” the popular duo predicted in an announcement on Tuesday. “We have wished to play the Ugly Sisters for so many years, it feels this is the fulfilment of a dream – a dream our hearts made.”

headlinePool.title: Danes vote as PM Mette Frederiksen seeks third term after Greenland boost
headlinePool.description: Frederiksen enjoyed a surge in popularity for standing up to the US over Greenland but her support is down on 2022.

headlinePool.title: US park police officer wounded in ‘ambush’ shooting in Washington DC
headlinePool.description: Park police chief says officer was ‘ambushed’ by two gunmen who fired as officer drove in unmarked vehicle A US park police officer was seriously wounded on Monday evening in a shooting in Washington DC in what the park police chief called an ambush. The park police chief, Scott Brecht, said in a press briefing that the unidentified officer was “ambushed” by two gunmen who fired at the officer as he drove by in an unmarked vehicle. The officer was working on a park police investigation when he was shot. The chief declined to give specifics of the investigation.
